title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Leah Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard processes, runbooks, and artifacts used by Redwood Inference Customer Success (CS) and Support for enterprise onboarding. It covers: the pre-onboarding checklist, integration guide highlights, escalation paths and SLAs, known issues and workarounds, routine health checks, and a QBR (Quarterly Business Review) template. Use this document as the single source of truth for consistent customer onboarding and post-onboarding operations.

Owners & Contacts

- Document owner: Customer Success (owner: Leah Martinez)
- Primary CS contact: leah.martinez@redwood.ai
- Escalation Slack channel: #cs-enterprise-escalations (monitored 24x7 by oncall support and CS on-call)
- Support escalation email: enterprise-support@redwood.ai
- Oncall rotation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (see runbook for paging policy)

Scope

- Applies to enterprise customers onboarding onto Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Not a substitute for detailed engineering runbooks (see eng-sre and eng-private-deployments pages).

Pre-onboarding checklist (CS responsibilities)

1. Contract & access
   - Verify contract type (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and SLAs.
   - Confirm signed security addenda (if required) and KMS/HSM configuration windows.
   - Create customer workspace in Console and provision initial API key in a sandbox project.

2. Technical prerequisites (completed before integration kick-off)
   - Network: For Private/Dedicated, validate VPC peering / VPN details and CIDR ranges.
   - IAM: Confirm SSO provider and mapping, RBAC roles for 3 initial users.
   - Data: Identify sample datasets and PII handling expectations, confirm retention policy.

3. Operational prep
   - Define success metrics (latency SLO, error budget tolerance, throughput targets). Typical baseline: 99.9% availability, median inference latency < 200 ms for text generation on hosted small/med models.
   - Schedule kickoff meeting with CS, Solutions Engineering, and customer stakeholders.

Onboarding runbook (30/60/90-day milestones)

- Day 0–7: Kickoff & discovery
  - Deliverables: Kickoff deck, customer architecture diagram, integration plan
  - Actions: Confirm API keys, create test prompts, run basic smoke tests (see Integration checklist)
- Week 2–4: Integration & validation
  - Deliverables: Staging integration, performance baseline report, security checklist complete
  - Actions: Run load tests (see Benchmark section), validate streaming and function-calling if used
- Month 1–3: Stabilization & enablement
  - Deliverables: Monitoring dashboard configured, runbook handed to customer ops, first monthly health summary
  - Actions: Tune batching/quantization recommendations, perform failover drills for model routing

Integration guide (developer-focused highlights)

- API endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/rerank (refer to API doc for full param list).
- Common SDKs: python (redwood.inference.Client), go, and node (official SDKs).
- Recommended test flow:
  1) Sanity call to /v1/generate using a short prompt and timeout=5s
  2) Validate streaming responses with sdk.stream() and fallback to polling if not supported
  3) Confirm metrics emitted to customer dashboard (tokens/generated, latency p50/p95, error rate)
- Batching and caching: Enable prefix-KV cache for high-reuse prompt families; recommend max_batch_size 16 for CPU-backed Dedicated GPUs initially.

Integration checklist (table-like bullets)

- Network connectivity: VPN or peering validated? (yes/no)
- Auth: SSO mapped and test user created? (yes/no)
- Secrets: KMS keys provisioned (Private) or API key rotation policy agreed? (yes/no)
- Observability: Dashboards linked and alerts configured? (yes/no)
- Performance: Baseline load test results uploaded? (yes/no)

Escalation playbook

Severity definitions
- Sev1 (P1): Production outage impacting all users (total service unavailable, or error rate > 10% above baseline for > 5 minutes).
- Sev2 (P2): Degraded service impacting a significant subset of users (latency spike p95 > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes).
- Sev3 (P3): Partial impact or non-critical functionality broken (rate-limit misconfig, SDK bug).
- Sev4 (P4): Minor issues, feature requests, or questions.

Escalation steps (fast path)
1. Triage in Support (within 15 minutes for P1/P2): confirm customer, environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and reproduce or collect logs.
2. Notify CS and SRE oncall in #cs-enterprise-escalations (immediate for P1).
3. If P1: page Eng SRE (pager duty), start incident channel #incident-<customer>-<date>, and assign incident commander.
4. For Dedicated/Private: add infra contact and account engineering.
5. Post-incident: produce a 72-hour summary and schedule an RCA if customer requests or if SLO breached.

SLA and response objectives (CS & Support)
- Acknowledgement targets: P1 within 15 minutes, P2 within 60 minutes, P3 within 4 business hours, P4 within 2 business days.
- Investigation/update cadence: 30 minutes for P1 until mitigation, hourly for P2.
- Resolution windows are customer-specific and documented in contract; aim to restore service within 4 hours for typical P1s on Hosted.

Known issues & workarounds (living list)

- Tokenization mismatch for multilingual prompts (reported 2025-08): Workaround: normalize input using redwood.text.normalize_unicode() and enforce model-specific tokenizer via header Model-Tokenizer: utf8-v1.
- Streaming dropouts during large-batch inferencing on older GPU families: Workaround: reduce max_batch_size to 8 and enable keepalive on HTTP/2. Patch scheduled in runtime v1.12.2.
- Rate-limit bursts causing 429s for background jobs: Workaround: implement client-side exponential backoff and use reserved per-route burst tokens for Dedicated customers.

Health checks & QBR material

Monthly health check checklist (CS -> Customer)
- Key metrics: monthly active requests, average tokens per request, p50/p95 latency, 5xx error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
- Alert summary: list active alerts in last 30 days and actions taken.
- Performance anomalies: any regressions from model rollouts or quantization changes.
- Recommendations: batching/cache/quantization config adjustments and cost-optimization suggestions.

QBR template (30–45 minutes)
1. Attendees & objectives (5 min)
2. Last quarter outcomes and SLA summary (5–8 min)
3. Usage & cost trends (8–10 min)
4. Performance and quality metrics (p50/p95 latencies, error trends, eval regressions) (8–10 min)
5. Roadmap & upcoming changes (models, runtime patches, planned maintenance) (5–7 min)
6. Action items and success metrics for next quarter (5 min)

Templates & artifacts (links to canned assets)
- Kickoff deck (template): /assets/cs/kickoff-deck-template.pptx
- Integration test suite: /repos/cs/integration-tests/README.md
- QBR slide template: /assets/cs/qbr-template.pptx

Post-onboarding handoff

- Deliver final Health Check report and Runbook to customer (PDF).
- Ensure ownership transfer: CS -> Customer Ops and Support -> SRE/Platform for Dedicated/Private.
- Confirm training completed for customer users (admin, devs, ops).

Change history & governance

- Major updates to this playbook must be approved by Customer Success leadership and reviewed by Eng-SRE and Solutions Engineering.
- Review cadence: annually or after any major process change (incidents that led to SLA changes).

Appendix: Runbook snippets and CLI commands

- Smoke test example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":16}'

- Basic load test guidance: use k6 or locust against a staging endpoint with a target RPS equal to 1.5x expected production throughput. Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies.

If you have questions about this playbook, contact the owner or open a thread in #cs-docs for proposed edits.
